column1: # R1654 — the text-smear ratchet's budget. One row per example whose painted
# text runs land on each other: two runs of ONE widget overlapping is the
# signature of a run that FLOWED instead of being placed (a TextNode's rect
# reads like a position and is not one), or of a box narrower than the string
# it promised, where the second line lands on the row below.
# The gate (tools/rpc_verify.py, at every demo's boot) reads `scene/text_painted`
# — the only surface that reports a run's window rectangle, because a run carries
# no tag and every other read in this tree is tag-keyed. A COUNT per example
# rather than a list of pairs: the identity of a pair is a rectangle and
# rectangles move, so pinning the pairs would make an unrelated layout change
# A number may be LOWERED by the round that repairs the screen and must never be
# raised to make a failure go away — that is the one use that turns a ratchet
# headless here at all (terminal arms, an audio-device demo, a couple that exit
# at boot) and are unmeasured rather than clean. Taken BEFORE the settings-form
# painter gained its overflow policy in the same round, so a handful of these
# numbers are an upper bound on what the tree does now — which is the safe
